title: Findings in Academic Freedom Survey 2021 by AcademiaSG
what_it_is: Findings in Academic Freedom Survey 2021 by AcademiaSG

sections.label: Academic Freedom Survey Response Rate
sections.summary: The survey had about a 10% response rate, with only a minority of respondents reporting significant concerns about academic freedom in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: With regard to the Academic Freedom Survey by AcademiaSG, the authors of the survey have noted that the response rate was only about 10%, that is, about 198 out of 2,061 contacted academics in the social sciences, humanities, business and law schools at the National University of Singapore (NUS), the Nanyang Technological University (NTU), the Singapore Management University (SMU), the Singapore University of Technology and Design (SUTD) and the Singapore University of Social Sciences (SUSS) replied to the survey.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: Among the 10% who responded, only a minority reported significant concerns about academic freedom in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: I would, therefore, advise some caution in generalising the findings from the survey as representative of how all academics in Singapore feel.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: Academics in AUs have been able to teach, engage in discourse, research and publish on a wide range of topics, including domestic politics, race, religion and gender issues.

sections.label: NUS Singapore-related publications listing
sections.summary: NUS' Faculty of Arts and Social Sciences publicly lists more than 8,000 Singapore-related publications, with more being added over time.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: The NUS' Faculty of Arts and Social Sciences has a public listing of more than 8,000 Singapore-related publications, with more being added over time.

sections.label: MOE funded sensitive-topic projects
sections.summary: MOE has funded projects on potentially sensitive topics under competitive grants, many led by female researchers.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: MOE has also funded projects on topics that may be considered sensitive, under the competitive grants.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: Examples include integration of bi-national families in Singapore, coping strategies among low-income households and the development of racial attitudes during early childhood.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: Many of these projects are led by female researchers.
